newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet : lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
COLOMBO POLICE STATIONS TO HAVE CITIZENS' COMMITTEES

Citizens' committee will be set up in every police area in Colombo to minimise inconvenience to Tamils taken in during raids for Liberation tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told Parliament. The committees will assist police in checking the bonafies of Tamils and release the innocent people within three hours, he added.
SUDDEN AFFLUENCE OF TELECOM WORKERS

Some of Sri Lanka Telecom workers turned millionaires overnight with the issue of 3.5 percent shares to the workers based on the number of years of service they have put in with the organisation. Even the newest of employees will own shares worth over 100,000 rupees, said Posts, Telecommunications and Media Minister Mangala Samarweera.
THE ISLAND
GOVT SAYS 300,000 NEW TELEPHONES IN TWO YEARS

The government has been assured by Nippon Telegraphic and Telephone Corporation Ltd. (NTT), strategic partner of Sri Lanka Telecom, that the backlog of 300,000 telephone connections will be cleared in two years, said director general of Public Enterprise Reforms Commission (PERC) Mano Tittawella. The NTT will infuse $300 million in addition to the equity capital of $225 million to upgrade the technology and to meet the increased demand for telephones.
LAWMAKERS WORRIED OVER IMPORT OF INDIAN LABOUR

Sri Lanka lawmakers have expressed concern over import of some 600 Indian workers by an Indian firm which has been contracted to extend overhead power lines in the island. Kalutara district lawmaker Tilak Karunaratne has asked the relevant ministry to send the Indian workers back and instead employ local labour.
DIVAINA, VIRAKESARI & DINAMINA
"JAYA SIKURU" FORCES LINK UP NEAR PULIYANKULAM

Two columns of "Jaya Sikuru" troops advancing from different directions linked up on Wednesday near Puliyankulam, military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said. One column was advancing from Nedunkeni and the other from Omanthai. By this link up the army has been able to establish a security zone covering Omanthai, Parayanalankulam, Puliyankulam and Nedunkeni areas, strengthening security for Weli Oya and Vavuniya Town.
THINAKARAN & THINAKKURUL
NEW HIGH COURT TO TRY ANTI-TERRORIST DETAINEES

An additional High Court mainly for hearing cases under the Prevention of Terrorism Act is to start functioning from August 15, Minister of Justice Gamini Peiris told a press conference. The court is being opened mainly for hearing cases under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.
LANKADEEPA
MINISTER ORDERS PROBE INTO PORT RECRUITMENTS

Minister of Port Development, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction, Mohammed Ashraff has ordered an immediate investigation into all recruitments to Sri Lanka Ports Authority after the present government came into power. This follows complaints about alleged frauds and malpractices in appointments. About 4,183 persons have been appointed in the past three years in violation of stipulated recruitment procedures, the port trade union has said.
LSSP PROTESTS AGAINST SALE OF TELECOM

The LSSP General Secretary, Batty Weerakoon, has written to President Chandriuka Kumaratunga protesting against the sale of 35 percent of Sri Lanka Telecom shares to Japan's NTT. Weerakoon said the sale was not in the national interest and his party did not agree with Telecom's privatisation.
DIVAINA
FEARED PADDY PEST IN SRI LANKA

Sri Lanka's Environment Study Circle has said that that paddy pest "Apple Snail" had spread to seven districts of the country and was threatening the crop. This snail was first brought into Sri Lanka to develop the ornamental fish industry.
THINAKKURUL
ADB OFFICE IN COLOMBO

Asian Development Bank will open an office in Colombo in October, Mangala Samaraweera, Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and Media said. This will facilitate the Bank to have close contact with the government and speedily study proposed development projects. ADB has assisted many large projects in the past in a big way, he added.
